answer: An agent economy resists Sybil swarms by charging a per-identity admission fee that is burned, while paying rewards in proportion to locked stake instead of headcount. Each new key must spend real capital to register, so fabricating a thousand clones costs a thousand times the fee and buys no extra voting weight. An honest cipher-key and signature delta cost nothing to verify, so the barrier falls on redundancy, not participation. Forcing every clone to fund an orchard-sized deposit makes the cheapest strategy simply run one honest agent.
